content.value_statement: Startup teams need clear market evidence before choosing segments, competitors, and entry strategy. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured market intelligence workflows.
actual_capabilities: Sizes markets with TAM, SAM, and SOM methods.
Prioritizes customer segments by size, urgency, accessibility, and willingness to pay.
Maps direct, indirect, and future competitors into a comparison matrix.
Assesses market growth, timing, consolidation, and disruption signals.
Scores opportunities and recommends next validation actions.
Connects market findings to related startup planning workflows.
limitations: Does not fetch live market data unless the host AI tool has browsing enabled.
Outputs depend on the quality of user inputs and cited sources.
Market estimates are directional and require validation with customer research.
Does not replace legal, financial, or investment advice.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a New Market
use_cases.description: Estimate market size, customer segments, competitors, and timing before investing product resources.

use_cases.title: Refresh Quarterly Intelligence
use_cases.description: Update competitive moves, segment performance, and opportunity scores for planning cycles.

use_cases.title: Compare Pivot Options
use_cases.description: Score alternative markets by attractiveness, competitive intensity, and execution fit.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Market Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new product idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [product idea] in [geography] and [industry]. Estimate TAM, SAM, SOM, top segments, competitors, and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Competitive Landscape
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the top five competitors for [product idea]. Compare positioning, strengths, weaknesses, pricing, funding, and differentiation opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Customer Segment Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile the best customer segments for [product idea]. Rank them by size, pain severity, urgency, accessibility, and willingness to pay.

prompt_templates.title: Go or No-Go Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a full opportunity score for [market option]. Include market attractiveness, competitive position, execution fit, key risks, assumptions, and validation experiments.

output_examples.input: AI personal finance coaching for Gen Z in the United States.
output: Market size estimate with confidence rating.
Prioritized customer segments and entry segment.
Three validation actions for the next two weeks.

output_examples.input: Quarterly market update after six months of enterprise traction.
output: Revised segment performance and market assumptions.
New competitor moves and emerging threats.
Updated opportunity score and planning recommendations.

output_examples.input: Decision support for a possible pivot from B2C to B2B SaaS.
output: Execution fit assessment for the current team.
Go, no-go, or investigate further recommendation.

best_practices: Use both top-down and bottom-up sizing methods.
Document each assumption and source behind market numbers.
Validate findings with customer interviews and buying behavior.
anti_patterns: Treating TAM as revenue that is immediately reachable.
Analyzing every competitor instead of the most relevant ones.
Using unvalidated customer statements as purchase evidence.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide the product idea, target geography, and industry vertical. Add assumptions, constraints, and strategy context when available.

faq.question: Can it perform live research?
faq.answer: It can structure research prompts and analysis. Live data depends on the AI tool and available browsing.

faq.question: Does it create financial forecasts?
faq.answer: It creates market and opportunity estimates. It does not replace formal financial modeling or investment advice.

faq.question: How should TAM, SAM, and SOM be used?
faq.answer: Use them as directional estimates. Validate each assumption with credible sources and customer evidence.

faq.question: Can it compare competitors?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares direct, indirect, and future competitors by positioning, pricing, strengths, gaps, and threats.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
